item.title: Fashion Briefing: Fashion designers spoke out against ICE at New York Fashion Week
item.description: One of the most commonly spotted accessories at New York Fashion Week this season wasn't a handbag or a pair of sunglasses — it was a small black-and-white pin featuring the words "ICE OUT."

item.title: How Clarins reached 70% conversion and doubled its basket size in brick-and-mortar test of shade-matching tech
item.description: Clarins, the 72-year-old French heritage cosmetics brand, has found a sweet spot between AI-powered technology and in-person customer service. In 2025, it quietly launched a beta test called Clarins AI Shade Finder developed in collaboration with IlluminateAI, a Silicon Valley deep-tech start up that emerged from stealth in August of last year. Thanks to its success, Clarins is now rolling out the advisor-assisted tech to 200 locations.

item.title: Luxury Briefing: How 2 designers weighed the costs vs. the benefits of an NYFW show
item.description: In this week’s Luxury Briefing, a look at the brand strategies behind Simkhai’s and PatBo’s show formats at New York Fashion Week. Plus, data on the NYFW styles inspiring shoppers.

item.title: A buyer’s take on New York Fashion Week, with Printemps New York’s Silvano Vangi
item.description: This week, with New York Fashion Week wrapped up, the Glossy Podcast is joined by Silvano Vangi, creative and merchandising director at Printemps New York, to get a buyer's perspective on this season's NYFW.

item.title: Glossy Pop Newsletter: Inside Hello’s plan to make toothpaste part of Gen Z’s beauty routine
item.description: Toothpaste is one of the most predictable products in personal care: a minty paste in a tube, designed for efficacy over experience. But as Gen Z increasingly looks to upgrade every part of their daily routines, and as GRWM-style content spills into non-beauty categories, oral care is entering a cute new era.

item.title: Exclusive: Bath & Body Works launches on Amazon
item.description: The mall store isn’t dead — it has just gone online. The Ohio-based personal care brand will now sell its famed body mists and candles to Amazon U.S. customers as part of a larger turnaround plan to meet consumers where they're at.

item.title: Fashion brands are ‘cautiously optimistic’ about the Supreme Court striking down many of Trump’s tariffs
item.description: On Friday, the Supreme Court dealt a significant blow to the administration's efforts to enact sweeping tariffs on imports from nearly every country in the world. The Court's 6-3 ruling found that tariffs enacted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, which covers many but not all of the tariffs, were unlawful and that the president exceeded his authority.

item.title: Jewlery has a London Fashion Week moment amid gold and silver pricing concerns
item.description: London’s jewelry brands are turning precious metal volatility into stronger margins, urgency and bespoke growth.

item.title: 3 standout strategies driving Revlon’s 2026 comeback plan
item.description: Revlon is betting on bold color as it refocuses its brands in 2026 under CEO Melissa Peluso. That includes refreshes at Revlon, Almay, American Crew, Elizabeth Arden and Juicy Couture fragrances, among other brands. Glossy sat down with the executive 16 months into her tenure to learn about the tactics and strategies driving the brand’s turnaround effort.

item.title: Sephora Strategies: What MAC needs to succeed at Sephora
item.description: MAC has long since been available in international Sephora markets like Canada and the U.K. But with a new creative director in Nicola Formichetti, fresh talent like pop star Chappell Roan and a rebounding makeup category hungry for color, MAC has earned a place at Sephora's U.S. fleet. And with MAC's parent company The Estée Lauder Companies still finding its footing in makeup, a diversified retail presence at a global powerhouse like Sephora is as important as ever.
